description: Two-panel composite figure (Fig. 5). (a) Instrumented Charpy load-displacement curves: x-axis "Displacement/mm" (0 to ~9, ticks 0-8), y-axis "Loading/N" (0-18000, ticks every 6000), legend MHT (black), S1050 (blue), S1000 (red). The red S1000 curve rises fastest and peaks between the 12000 and 18000 N gridlines, then drops steeply near 2 mm displacement; the blue S1050 curve peaks later and slightly lower, decaying to near zero by ~7 mm; the black MHT curve shows the broadest, lowest peak (about 2.5-3 mm) with the longest gradual decay, staying above the other two beyond 4 mm and extending to ~8.5 mm. An inset shows the Charpy specimen geometry, 55 mm x 10 mm x 5 mm, with a notch and a red RD (rolling direction) arrow. (b) Stacked bar chart of Impact Energy/J (y-axis 0-70, ticks every 10) for S1000, S1050 and MHT, each bar split into blue hatched crack propagation energy above red hatched crack initiation energy, with error bars; the legend prints "Crack propagataion energy/J" and "Crack inititaion energy/J". Total bar height increases S1000 < S1050 < MHT. Together the panels show that the higher total impact energy of MHT arises mainly from greater crack propagation energy, indicating a longer, more energy-consuming crack path.

subfigures.description: Instrumented Charpy load-displacement curves, Loading/N (0-18000) vs Displacement/mm (0-9), for MHT (black), S1050 (blue) and S1000 (red). S1000 peaks first and highest and drops steeply near 2 mm; MHT peaks lowest/latest and decays most slowly, extending to ~8.5 mm. Inset: Charpy specimen schematic, 55 mm x 10 mm x 5 mm with notch and red RD arrow.

Stacked bar chart of Impact Energy/J (0-70) for S1000, S1050 and MHT, with blue hatched crack propagation energy stacked on red hatched crack initiation energy and error bars; total energy increases S1000 < S1050 < MHT. Legend contains the printed typos 'Crack propagataion energy/J' and 'Crack inititaion energy/J'.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots Loading/N (y, 0-18000, ticks at 0, 6000, 12000, 18000) against Displacement/mm (x, 0 to ~9, ticks at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8) for three curves labelled S1000 (red), S1050 (blue) and MHT (black).
The red S1000 load-displacement curve peaks between the 12000 and 18000 N gridlines at the smallest displacement and then falls steeply to a low, fluctuating level near 2 mm displacement.
The black MHT curve has the broadest and lowest maximum, remains above the S1050 and S1000 curves beyond ~4 mm displacement, and extends furthest along the displacement axis (to ~8.5 mm).
An inset in panel (a) is a Charpy specimen schematic dimensioned 55 mm (length), 10 mm (width) and 5 mm (thickness), with a machined notch and a red arrow labelled RD marking the rolling direction.

Panel (b) is a stacked bar chart with y-axis 'Impact Energy/J' from 0 to 70 (ticks every 10) and three bars labelled S1000, S1050 and MHT; each bar is split into blue hatched crack propagation energy on top of red hatched crack initiation energy, and each bar carries an error bar.
In panel (b) the total bar height increases in the order S1000 (below the 30 J gridline) < S1050 (just above the 40 J gridline) < MHT (about midway between the 50 and 60 J gridlines).
The (b) legend text is printed with typographical errors exactly as 'Crack propagataion energy/J' (blue hatch) and 'Crack inititaion energy/J' (red hatch).
The caption states that (a) shows load-displacement curves and (b) shows energy absorbed for crack initiation and energy absorbed for crack propagation at three different heat treatment temperatures.
The citing text states the total impact energies are 29.2 J for S1000, 42.8 J for S1050 and 55.1 J for MHT, an increase of 88.6% for MHT relative to S1000.

The citing text states the crack propagation energy rises from 9.87 J for S1000 to 26.64 J for S1050 and to 36.78 J for MHT, and that the difference in impact energy between the specimens is mainly due to the crack propagation energy.
The citing text states the displacements of S1000, S1050 and MHT are 4.55, 6.30 and 8.04 mm respectively.
The citing text states the crack initiation energy of S1050 is slightly lower than that of S1000 and MHT, the latter two having comparable crack initiation energies.
The citing text states MHT shows a 29% increase in impact toughness compared with S1050, attributed to larger grain size and more special boundaries forcing crack deflection.

One citing sentence refers to the crack initiation and crack propagation energies as being in 'Fig. 5(a and b)', while the caption assigns the energies to (b) and the load-displacement curves to (a); the energy-stacking bar chart is in the panel labelled (b).
